question.text: According to the German high-rise building regulations: (a) above what height of the uppermost floor (on one side of the building, above ground level) does a building intended for long-term human occupation count as a high-rise building, and (b) what minimum walking width must each of the emergency stairs have in a high-rise building up to 60 m high?
source: High-rise buildings are those intended for long-term human occupation whose upper-most floor on one side of the building is more than 22 m above ground level.
High-rise buildings up to 60 m high: at least two emergency stairs must be available, which must be located opposite in two separate fire compartments. Their walking width must be at least 1.25 m.
context:
Definition of high-rise buildings
High-rise buildings are those intended for long-term human occupation whose upper-most floor on one side of the building is more than 22 m above ground level.

Stairs
High-rise buildings up to 60 m high: at least two emergency stairs must be available, which must be located opposite in two separate fire compartments. Their walking width must be at least 1.25 m. The wellhole must be min. 0.80 m wide in order to avoid having to lay hoses on the stairs. Smoke outlets must be provided at their highest point (5% of the floor area but min. 1 m^2). The exit must be directly into the open air or through a lobby without any fire load. In exceptional cases, one staircase can be approved for high-rise buildings up to 60 m in height, if it is a safety staircase. Requirements for the location of stairs → 2 – 5.

answer.text:
A high-rise building is defined by an uppermost occupied floor **more than 22 m above ground level**. For high-rises up to 60 m, each emergency stair must have a minimum walking width of **1.25 m**.

Answer: B

answer.text:
**(a)** A building counts as a high-rise (Hochhaus) when the floor of at least one storey usable for long-term occupation lies **more than 22 m** above the adjoining ground surface.

**(b)** Each required (emergency) staircase must have a usable walking width of at least **1.20 m** for its flights and landings. I believe this is the value in the Model High-Rise Directive (Muster-Hochhaus-Richtlinie) for high-rises up to 60 m, but I am less certain of it than of part (a).

answer.text:
**(a)** In Germany, a building counts as a high-rise (Hochhaus) when the floor of at least one room for long-term occupation is more than 22 m above ground level. This 22 m threshold is the standard one in the state building codes and the Muster-Hochhausrichtlinie. That rules out options C and D.

**(b)** I am less sure about the stair width. The current Muster-Hochhausrichtlinie gives a usable stair width of 1.20 m, which matches neither option. I recall that older high-rise regulations, as reproduced in references such as Neufert, required a walking width of at least 1.25 m. That is why I lean towards B over A, but this is from memory.

Answer: B
